# env-doc

Never write `.env.example` by hand again. Parses your codebase for environment variable references and auto-generates a `.env.example` file.

## Usage

```bash
# Generate .env.example in current directory
python env-doc.py

# Specify project root
python env-doc.py --path /path/to/project

# Write to a custom location
python env-doc.py --output /path/to/.env.example

# Print to stdout instead of writing
python env-doc.py --stdout
```

## Example Output

```
# Environment Variables
# Auto-generated by env-doc
# Source: src/db.py

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db
# Found in: src/db.py, src/config.py

API_KEY=your-api-key-here
# Found in: src/services/api.py

DEBUG=false
# Found in: src/main.py
```

## Supported Languages & Patterns

| Language | Patterns Scanned |
|----------|-----------------|
| Python   | `os.getenv()`, `os.environ[]`, `os.environ.get()` |
| Node/JS  | `process.env.VAR` |
| Rust     | `std::env::var()`, `env!("VAR")` |
| Go       | `os.Getenv()`, `os.LookupEnv()` |
| Shell    | `$VAR_NAME` in .sh, .bash, .zsh |
| Docker   | `$VAR_NAME` in Dockerfile |
| YAML     | `${VAR_NAME}` in .yml, .yaml |

## Options

| Flag            | Description                     |
|-----------------|---------------------------------|
| `--path`        | Project root (default: cwd)      |
| `--output`, `-o`| Output file (default: .env.example) |
| `--stdout`      | Print to stdout                  |
